key_insight: θ-TaN shows strong anisotropic tensile behavior, with higher strength along [0001] but greater ductility along [2-1-10], and it fractures by cleavage rather than dislocation-mediated plasticity.
engineering_relevance: These atomistic strength and fracture data help assess θ-TaN as a reliable high-thermal-conductivity material for device thermal management and interconnect applications.
method: Neuroevolution-potential molecular dynamics simulations of θ-TaN tensile loading
Size-convergence testing to select a 20 nm model length
Strain-rate and temperature sweeps to quantify mechanical anisotropy and thermal effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports <3.5% variation in mechanical parameters across 10^7–10^9 s^-1 strain rates, with strength/modulus values differing by direction and retaining over 73% of 300 K strength at 900 K.
watch_item: Results come from simulation-scale loading rates and idealized crystals, so real microstructure, defects, and experimental fracture behavior may differ.
paper_title: Anisotropic Tensile Strength and Fracture Mechanism of $θ$-TaN: A Machine-Learning Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
